title: A resource for assessing dynamic binary choices in the adult brain using EEG and mouse-tracking
description: This dataset provides high-density (128-channel) EEG and mouse-tracking data from 31 adults aged 18-33, collected in 2020. It includes resting-state recordings and task recordings from food preference choices and semantic judgments. The resource is intended for studying the dynamic decision processes underlying binary choices in the human brain.
methods_description: EEG was recorded with a 128-channel EGI system (10/20-based cap) at a 1000 Hz sampling rate, with E129 (Cz) as reference and electrode impedances kept below 50 kohm. Participants completed resting-state recordings and two mouse-tracking tasks (food preference choices and semantic judgments). The dataset includes raw .mff files, BIDS-formatted .set files, PsychoPy stimulus scripts, and EEGLAB-preprocessed continuous data.
